'''Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game''' is the third Star Wars CCG product, published in February 1996 by Decipher with Parker Brothers.<ref>[https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Premiere_Two-Player_Introductory_Set Premiere Two-Player Introductory Set], Wookieepedia. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260308164354/https://starwars.fandom.com/wiki/Premiere_Two-Player_Introductory_Set Internet Archive]</ref> It contains six exclusive white-border premium cards (3 Light, 3 Dark), two 60-card preconstructed white-border decks, a rules booklet and one Premiere booster pack. Its MSRP was $19.95. The first ~50,000 boxes had a Limited Premiere pack; later boxes had Unlimited. Europe used a Waddingtons flip-top box, and Takara published a Japanese version.<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2]; online edition: [https://www.starwarsccg.org/collecting/ SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia], starwarsccg.org. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261022023930/https://swccg.com/snapshots/pc/collecting.html Internet Archive]</ref>

A Spanish-language rules booklet was prepared for a Spanish SWCCG release that was later cancelled; see [[Spanish Premiere Two-Player Game rules booklet]] and [[Translations of SWCCG]]. A German-language two-player rulebook printed by Modern Graphics is among the surviving artifacts of a planned German SWCCG release that was later cancelled; see [[Cancelled German release of SWCCG]].

The rules booklet thanks [[Richard Borg]] "for rogue design in an elegant system".<ref name="2p-credits">[https://www.hasbro.com/common/instruct/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game.PDF Introductory Two-Player Game Rules Booklet], Decipher / Parker Brothers, credits page. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015192404/https://www.hasbro.com/common/instruct/Star_Wars_Customizable_Card_Game.PDF Internet Archive]</ref>

Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009010838/https://arstechnica.com/gaming/2015/12/that-one-time-i-played-in-the-star-wars-card-game-world-championship/ Internet Archive]</ref>

According to former Decipher volunteer [[Jim Colson]], the packaging was the same everywhere, but the booster packs inside depended on where the box was sold. Copies sold through Kmart and Walmart held white-border packs; copies sold through hobby shops held black-border packs.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PRRkRBHlo-o&t=3116s Star Wars CCG INSIDER Stories, History & Collector Tips from the legend Jim Colson], BoardMatt, YouTube (uploaded 24 April 2022), at 51:56. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-PRRkRBHlo-o Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG Insider Stories with Jim Colson (transcript)]].</ref> Decipher advertised the game on television with the tagline "The galaxy in a box".<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IXsMeCs8sZo&t=23s Star Wars CCG - TV Ad (1996)], Lusco-fusco, YouTube (uploaded 14 December 2020), at 00:23. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261023022207/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IXsMeCs8sZo&t=23s Internet Archive]. Transcript: [[Star Wars CCG TV Ad (1996) (transcript)]].</ref>

The card list below covers the six exclusive premiums; the randomized Premiere booster in the box is a reprint.

The booklet names 26 playtesters: [[Bill Martinson]], [[Mark Tuttle]], [[Darrell Budic]], [[Reg Schmeichel]], [[Sandy Wible]], [[Bob Madison]], [[Will Madison]], [[Sandy Borg]], [[Craig VanNess]], [[Chuck Kallenbach]], [[Cheryl Kallenbach]], [[Paul Sudlow]], [[Scott Willhelm]], [[Gary Mockus]], [[Shawn Smallman]], [[Rick Thomas]], [[Dick Heinz]], [[Dan Van Horn]], [[Jim Berhalter]], [[Peter McCarthy]], [[Kyle Roth]], [[Troy Pope]], [[Lance Campbell]], [[Brad Toney]], [[Don Cory]] and [[Suzy Wolf]].<ref name="2p-credits" />

The game is dedicated to [[Joseph Campbell]], "whose vision and guidance inspired a young writer to explore the depths of his imagination and create a myth for a generation in desperate need of heroes". The booklet credits the gameplay to [[Technical Game Services]]. [[Parker Brothers]] of Beverly, Massachusetts distributed the game, and Carta Mundi printed its cards in Belgium.<ref name="2p-credits" />
